selection.judge_all: all 22 candidates are judged fresh first (about $0.02 each)
selection.run_set: 14 asks: every candidate the fresh judge calls HEAVY, in candidate order (at most 7), then the remaining candidates in candidate order until there are 14. The candidate order interleaves diagnostic and descriptive asks, so the set is spread across both whatever the judge says.
selection.why_14: measured on this install's own traces, a LuxExperience analyst turn costs about $0.34-0.41 and a conversation turn about $0.18-0.22 (Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 per M; the Anthropic binding sends no cache_control, so every prompt token is billed). 14 pairs is about $8.4 + $0.45 of judgments, under the $10 ceiling with a margin; 20 would not fit.
selection.spend_stop: before each run, if spend so far + the remaining runs at $0.45 (deep) / $0.25 (quick) each would pass $9.60, the remaining asks are not run and are reported as not run

scoring_rule.unit: one ask: the quick arm's final answer against the deep arm's final answer (envelope headline + body; for the analyst, the report's headline, summary and findings) and the figures each states
scoring_rule.reference: for each ask, BEFORE either answer is read, the figure(s) the ask requests are computed by SQL against the warehouse (POST /query/run on the copy), with the approved metric definition where the connection has one; for a why-ask, the size of the change asked about and its split along the dimensions the ask names (platform/storefront, category, brand tier, reason, country when none is named) — the largest contributor is the reference driver

deep_worth_it_if_any.W1_number: the ask requests a figure or a part (each named part is listed before the run) that deep states correctly and quick does not state, or states wrongly. Correct = within 2% relative (0.5 pt for a rate) of the reference, under the approved definition or the definition the answer itself declares.
deep_worth_it_if_any.W2_cause: a why / what-drives / how-much-of ask: deep names a driver with its quantified contribution that matches the reference driver or a SQL check confirms, and quick names no quantified driver, or one the reference contradicts.
deep_worth_it_if_any.W3_premise: the ask's stated premise is false (a stated figure off by more than 2% / 0.5 pt) or the data cannot carry it (a known trap, a provisional period), and deep says so while quick answers as if it were true.

scoring_rule.quick_better_if: deep makes a W1/W2/W3-type error quick does not (deep wrong where quick right), or deep returns no answer where quick answered
scoring_rule.tie: everything else, including both right, both wrong, and both missing the same part
scoring_rule.who_judges: W1 and the premise half of W3 are deterministic against SQL. Whether a stated driver MATCHES the reference driver (W2), and whether an answer FLAGS a premise (W3), are read by a model: this agent (claude-opus-5-5), not blind to which arm wrote which answer; the sentence that decided each W is quoted per ask in the result so a person can overrule it.

calibration.label: y = 1 when the ask scores deep_better, else 0 (tie and quick_better are 0)
calibration.judge_predicts: heavy (treatment = investigation) means 'deep is worth it'
reported: the 2x2 of judged tier against y
Fisher exact test, one-sided (heavy enriches y=1)
AUC of p_heavy against y with a permutation p
ECE of the stated confidence in the chosen treatment against whether its tier matched y (the module's 10 bins)
calibration.better_than_chance: Fisher exact one-sided p < 0.05. With n = 14 this needs a near-clean split; the power is stated beside the number.
calibration.exploratory_not_decisive: the other levers (causal, intent = diagnose, steps_implied_score) against y, and the ask's kind (diagnostic / descriptive) against y, as the baseline a router would have to beat

decision_reading_for_cp3.supported: CP-3's premise holds only if BOTH (a) deep beats quick on at least 25% of the valid asks AND (b) the judge's tier predicts those asks better than chance by the test above
decision_reading_for_cp3.a_without_b: deep earns its cost on some asks but this judge cannot find which: CP-3 stays held; the next lever is the judge, not the router
decision_reading_for_cp3.not_a: deep rarely earns its ~2-4x cost on these asks: a router has little to gain on this path; CP-3 stays held
